brief: JPMorgan's security software earnings recap argues that accelerating AI adoption is expanding enterprise attack surfaces, turning next-generation security spending from discretionary to necessity-driven. Frontier models like Anthropic's Mythos can now autonomously discover and exploit vulnerabilities, collapsing mean time to exploit to negative 7 days and leaving patching further behind attackers; JPMorgan estimates this could add over $430bn to the three-year security TAM and drive a steeper adoption curve than the cloud or mobile transitions did. 2Q26 results showed this shifting from pure multiple expansion into actual demand and pipeline acceleration, evidenced by platformization, Flex pricing, and AI product monetization (Prisma AIRS, AIDR, Tenable One) across the security stack, plus margin gains from AI-driven cost cuts. Because sales cycles are long, JPMorgan expects the fundamental earnings impact to build through 4Q26 and accelerate into 2027, so most vendors stayed cautious on near-term guidance despite bullish pipeline commentary. JPMorgan emerges from earnings season incrementally positive on OKTA, PANW, CRWD, VRNS, and ZS specifically, while individual 2Q stock reactions ranged from CRWD +20% to CLBT -29%.
